official.deadline_note: The round closes at 3:00 PM UK time on 18 November 2026; the Head of Department statement, nominated referee statement and host organisation approval must also be completed in Flexi-Grant by that time.
official.application_cycle: 2027 round; fellowships are expected to commence between 1 October 2027 and 1 January 2028
official.status_note: The scheme page shows Status: Open, with the 2027 round open 22 September 2026 and closing 18 November 2026, and decisions by 30 June 2027.
benefits: Contribution to the Research Fellow's basic salary and associated on-costs as set by the host institution (80% contribution)
Directly allocated (including estates) and indirect costs (80% contribution)
Research expenses including consumables, equipment, travel and attendance/presentation at conferences (100% contribution)
Relocation and visa costs for the applicant and their dependants (partner and children), which can be requested in addition to the total grant cap of £703,800 over four years
A bespoke, free-to-access programme of mentoring, training and networking, plus up to £5,000 per year within the research budget for further technical training and career/professional development
Financial support for childcare costs arising from attending conferences, collaborative research visits or invited talks
eligibility: You self-identify as being from a Black heritage background according to the England and Wales Census 2021: Black African, Black Caribbean, Black Other, Mixed White and Black Caribbean, Mixed White and Black African, or other mixed background including Black African, Black Caribbean or Black Other
You are a UK national, or you have completed part of your education in the UK through your Undergraduate, Master's or PhD studies, or you hold/have held a postdoctoral researcher position in the UK
You have a PhD, or will have one by the time the funding starts, and have less than 24 months of full-time postdoctoral experience by the closing date (18 November 2026)
Your research is within the Royal Society's remit of natural sciences, including but not limited to biological research and biomedical sciences, chemistry, engineering, mathematics and physics
The fellowship must be held at a UK Higher Education Institution, UK Research Council Institute, not-for-profit Independent Research Organisation, or Public Sector Research Establishment

Applicants can be of any nationality; both UK and non-UK domiciled researchers who wish to conduct their research in the UK are eligible, and those requiring a visa are eligible to apply for a Global Talent Visa under the fast-track process of endorsement
requirements: Apply through Flexi-Grant, the Royal Society's application and grant management system; paper-based applications will not be accepted
All applicants must submit an ORCID identifier before their application is submitted

A UK Sponsor (an established independent researcher with experience of mentoring early career researchers) must be identified at the point of application; the Royal Society will not assist applicants in identifying a sponsor

Supporting statements from the UK Sponsor, Head of Department and one nominated referee must be completed in Flexi-Grant, and the host organisation's delegated approver must approve the application, all before the deadline
References must be submitted in English; a reference not in English will not be accepted and may render the application ineligible
Shortlisted applicants are invited to an in-person interview at the Royal Society (interviews scheduled 12-13 May 2027)
documents: Research proposal: maximum 3 sides of A4 as a PDF (portrait, Arial no smaller than size 10, name and heading on every page) or 1,500 words of plain text, with all images and references inside the page limit
Personal statement on career and research aspirations (maximum 500 words) and a full reverse-chronological career history with dates and part-time percentages

List of key publications (maximum 1,000 words, in three sections: refereed papers in primary journals, refereed contributions to symposia and compiled volumes, and preprints) and current/previous research funding
Scientific abstract (maximum 400 words) and lay summary understandable by a non-specialist (maximum 250 words)
Outline of data management and data sharing plan (maximum 200 words)
UK Sponsor statement of support as a PDF on headed paper including name, title and contact details; Head of Department statement and one nominated referee statement submitted through Flexi-Grant
Letter of support from your PhD supervisor (PDF only) if you have not yet completed your PhD

Letters of support from any named collaborators (no more than 1 side of A4); ethics permission certificate or letter in English if the research involves human participants, patients or tissue; fieldwork permission and specimen collection documents where applicable
selection_criteria: The ability of the individual to deliver the fellowship project and their potential to develop an independent research career, with a track record commensurate with actual research experience
The quality of the proposed research project and the likelihood of achieving its goals
The suitability of the host organisation and research environment, the proposed support for career development and the scientific suitability of the sponsor
coverage: Research Fellow's basic salary costs and associated on-costs as set by the host institution (80% contribution)
Directly allocated (including estates) and indirect costs (80% contribution)

Research expenses including consumables, equipment, travel and attendance/presentation at conferences (100% contribution); a minimum of £30,000 of research expenses per annum is expected within the total award value
Relocation and visa costs for the applicant and dependants (partner and children), which can be requested in addition to the total grant cap of £703,800 over four years if well justified
application_method: Register and log in to Flexi-Grant at grants.royalsociety.org
Complete the application form sections: applicant career summary, research proposal, data management, financial details and applicant declaration
Invite the UK Sponsor, Head of Department and nominated referee through the participants tab and confirm every participant's status shows 'complete'
Submit the application for host organisation approval before 3:00 PM UK time on 18 November 2026
official.application_route: Online only via Flexi-Grant (grants.royalsociety.org), with host organisation approval completed before the deadline
official.study_mode: Full-time; part-time working is possible for childcare, caring responsibilities or personal circumstances, costed at 1.0 FTE in the application and adjusted by agreement if awarded
official.citizenship_residency: UK nationals, or those who completed part of their education in the UK (Undergraduate, Master's or PhD) or hold/have held a UK postdoctoral researcher position; applicants of any nationality are eligible
official.international_eligibility: Yes - applicants of any nationality may apply, but the research must be conducted in the UK; those requiring a visa can seek Global Talent Visa fast-track endorsement
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Research must be within the Royal Society's remit of natural sciences; clinical or interventional research on humans, social sciences and humanities are not supported unless otherwise agreed. One additional award is funded by the Alzheimer's Society for applicants working in the area of dementia, excluding clinical and interventional studies on humans
official.research_requirement: A curiosity-led research proposal developed in collaboration with your Sponsor, with project title, abstract, lay summary, methodology, milestones/timescales and a data management and data sharing plan
official.duration: Four years; fellowships are expected to commence between 1 October 2027 and 1 January 2028
official.description: The Royal Society's Career Development Fellowship is a four-year postdoctoral research fellowship, run as a pilot for researchers from Black heritage backgrounds, that funds high-quality research in a UK institution alongside a comprehensive programme of mentoring, training and networking. The scheme is funded by the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (BIST) and Royal Society charitable funds, with one additional award supported by the Alzheimer's Society for dementia research.
official.region: United Kingdom (research must be conducted at a UK host institution)
official.english_requirement: No IELTS, TOEFL or medium-of-instruction score is published; references must be submitted in English, and a reference not in English will not be accepted and may render the application ineligible

not_confirmed: IELTS/TOEFL or medium-of-instruction English language requirement (not published on the scheme page or scheme notes)
Any published tuition statement (the scheme funds salary and research costs; no tuition wording is published)
verification.notes: Award cap, funding split, deadline, timetable and process verified on the Royal Society scheme page and the Career Development Fellowships 2027 scheme notes PDF, both on royalsociety.org.

applicant_utility.summary: This four-year Royal Society fellowship puts up to £703,800 behind an early-career researcher from a Black heritage background, but the Society only pays 80% of salary and on-costs and 80% of estates and indirect costs, so your host department must commit to covering the remaining share out of its own funds. The 2027 round shuts at 3:00 PM UK time on 18 November 2026, and you cannot submit until your sponsor, Head of Department and referee have each finished their sections in Flexi-Grant and the host's approver has signed off, so recruit those people in September rather than November. Historical success rates sit at 3-7%, shortlisting leads to an in-person interview, and the panel is deliberately broad, so a proposal that only impresses specialists will not survive the longlisting stage. Plan your budget around the expected minimum of £30,000 research expenses per year inside the cap.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A researcher from a Black heritage background with a UK degree or UK postdoc link, fewer than 24 months of postdoctoral experience, who already has an established UK academic willing to act as sponsor.
application_readiness_checklist: Verify before drafting that your self-identified heritage maps to one of the England and Wales Census 2021 categories listed in the scheme notes, and that your UK education or UK postdoc link is documented

Secure your UK sponsor, Head of Department and nominated referee early and confirm each has (or will create) a Flexi-Grant account, since the submit button stays hidden until all three show 'complete'
Register an ORCID iD if you do not have one, as it is mandatory at the submission stage, and load your career history and publications from it

Build the budget jointly with the host research office: request at least £30,000 of research expenses per year inside the £703,800 cap, justify the salary point, inflation rate and any single item of equipment over £25,000
Hold the research proposal to 3 sides of A4 with figures and references inside the page limit, and write the lay summary for a non-specialist panel member
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 3:00 PM UK cut-off on 18 November 2026 - late applications are not accepted and the Society takes no responsibility for emails lost to spam filters or wrong addresses
A sponsor, Head of Department or referee who accepts the invitation but never selects 'Save & Submit', leaving your application permanently unsubmittable
Proposing research outside the natural sciences remit, including clinical or interventional human studies, social sciences or humanities, which are excluded unless pre-agreed with the Grants Team
A referee who is also your sponsor, a named collaborator, a panel member or a Royal Society Council member, or references not written in English
Under-requesting research expenses or carrying unjustified inflation and costs, which weakens an otherwise competitive case
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The host institution must fund the remaining 20% of salary and on-costs and 20% of directly allocated and indirect costs; relocation and visa costs are only payable above the £703,800 cap where well justified, and there is no expectation of a permanent post at the end of the four years.
document_audit: The sponsor statement must be a PDF on headed paper carrying the sponsor's name, title and contact details - an informal email or unheaded letter does not meet the published format
If your PhD is not yet finished, upload the supervisor's letter of support as a PDF and be ready to evidence that you passed your viva with no or minor corrections before the fellowship starts
Named collaborators need one-side letters confirming only their role and commitment; ethics permission documents for work involving human participants, patients or tissue must be in English
Career history dates must be exact (DD/MM/YYYY) with part-time percentages declared, because the under-24-months eligibility test is calculated directly from what you enter
alerts: Interviews are scheduled 12-13 May 2027 at the Royal Society with outcomes notified by email in June 2027 and offer letters in early July 2027 - block that diary space as soon as you are shortlisted in April
The pilot is closed to specific Census 2021 Black heritage categories only; identifying with a different Census ethnic group makes you ineligible for this round
You cannot hold the CDF alongside another fellowship - if you win both you must resign one, and accepting a permanent post after the deadline requires you to resign it if awarded the CDF
Future rounds of the pilot are not yet confirmed, so treat the 2027 round as a scarce opportunity rather than an annual certainty
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete every form section in Flexi-Grant, confirm the sponsor, Head of Department and referee all show 'complete', submit for host organisation approval, and ensure the host's delegated approver approves before 3:00 PM UK time on 18 November 2026.
